topics.title: Florida’s 2026 Amendment 3: property-tax changes
topics.summary: The reported vote is above the approval threshold, but official certification remains pending.

status.label: Unofficial results
status.detail: Results are not yet certified. A scheduled certification date does not establish certification.

topics.appliesTo: Florida owners and people establishing homestead; residence timing affects eligibility.

facts.text: Unofficial November 3, 2026 results show 61.98% Yes, above the required 60%.
State certification is scheduled for November 17, 2026 at 8 a.m.

If approved, changes begin January 1, 2027. Qualifying people with permanent Florida residence as of December 31, 2026 who establish homestead could receive non-school assessed-value exemptions up to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028.

People establishing Florida permanent residence from January 1, 2027 who establish homestead follow a separate phase-in: initially up to $50,000, with the higher exemption potentially available from their fifth exemption year.
The nonhomestead annual assessment-growth cap would fall from 10% to 5%.
These exemption amounts are not dollar-for-dollar tax savings and do not apply to school levies.

actions.text: Confirm homestead eligibility and residence dates with the county property appraiser.

topics.title: Condo reserves, inspections and assessments
topics.summary: A monthly condo fee does not show every future ownership cost. Review inspection findings, reserves and funding decisions together.

status.label: Owner checklist
status.detail: Requirements and timing depend on the building and association. Confirm applicable obligations with the association and its qualified advisers.

topics.appliesTo: Florida condominium owners and buyers, particularly in buildings subject to structural inspection and reserve-study requirements.

facts.text: A Structural Integrity Reserve Study (SIRS) estimates covered components' remaining life and costs and recommends a funding schedule.
A milestone inspection evaluates the building's structure. It serves a different purpose from the reserve study.
Funding can involve regular assessments, special assessments, loans or lines of credit under the statute's conditions. Review the association's actual plan.
Inspection reports and reserve studies belong in the association's records. Obtain current versions when reviewing a unit.

actions.text: Request the latest SIRS, milestone reports, adopted budget, reserve balances and funding plan.
Ask about approved or proposed assessments, borrowing, payment dates and planned repairs.
Bring your document questions to a property consultation.

topics.title: Citizens flood-insurance requirement
topics.summary: Citizens is expanding its flood-insurance requirement for affected new and renewing policies.

status.label: 2027 phase scheduled
status.detail: The next phase begins January 1, 2027. Confirm your policy's requirements with your insurance agent.

topics.appliesTo: Citizens personal residential policies with wind coverage, subject to stated exclusions.

facts.text: Affected policies for homes inside a Special Flood Hazard Area already require flood insurance.
Outside that area, the 2026 threshold is Coverage A of at least $400,000. From January 1, 2027, the requirement covers all insured values.
Condominium unit-owner policies, tenant contents policies and policies excluding windstorm or hail are exempt from this Citizens requirement.

actions.text: Ask your agent to check policy type, wind coverage, flood zone, Coverage A and renewal date.
Compare flood coverage and costs before renewal or closing.
